rulings.quote: the AIC data-collection and GEMM-validation runs pin the GPU clocks (SM \SI{2407}{\mega\hertz}, memory \SI{14001}{\mega\hertz})
rulings.evidence: The question IS decidable now. collector_artifacts/phaseE_physical_anchor/ENCODER_ANCHOR_SUMMARY.md:92 records the actual intervention: 'The user locked the clock (nvidia-smi -lgc 2400,2400 -lmc 14001) -> settled at SM 2392 / MEM 13801'. So the requested SM was 2400, not 2407, and the delivered memory clock was 13801, not 14001. 2407 MHz is the RTX 5090 boost-spec figure used as the AIC cost-model clock assumption (verify-fabel.md:26 quotes the AIC yaml comment '170 SM x 2407 MHz'); phaseB_batch_validation/bench_vit_batches.py:13 calls it 'the 2407 MHz lock reference', i.e. a reference, not an achieved pin. DB: `select distinct sm_clock_mhz from provenance.collector_encoder_fn order by 1;` -> 2377, 2385, 2392, 2400, 2887. No archived reading is 2407, and phaseB's own measured_f_n.csv sm_clock_mhz column reads 2377-2400. The memory clock 14001 IS the value passed to -lmc, so that half is the requested (not delivered) figure.
rulings.final_fix: Replace 'pin the GPU clocks (SM \SI{2407}{\mega\hertz}, memory \SI{14001}{\mega\hertz})' with: 'pin the GPU clocks via \texttt{nvidia-smi -lgc 2400,2400 -lmc 14001} (delivered SM 2377--2400\,\si{\mega\hertz}, MEM \SI{13801}{\mega\hertz}; the AIC cost model itself is parameterised at the \SI{2407}{\mega\hertz} boost reference)'. Justification: ENCODER_ANCHOR_SUMMARY.md:92; collector_encoder_fn.sm_clock_mhz distinct values.

rulings.quote: The foundation-model rows are uniformly near-white --- within a few percent of the per-cell optimum everywhere --- while the baseline rows darken as bins shrink.
rulings.evidence: Query: `with c as (select variate,resolution,model,mode,wape from provenance.forecast_metrics where candidate='point' and h=-1 and span='common'), b as (select variate,resolution,min(wape) bw from c group by 1,2) select c.resolution,c.model,max(round((c.wape/b.bw)::numeric,3)) from c join b using(variate,resolution) group by 1,2;` Per-model MAX rel-to-column-best: toto <=1.006 everywhere; chronos <=1.030 everywhere; timesfm 1.010 (1min), 1.030 (30s), 1.032 (45s), 1.056 (15s) but **1.220 (1s)** -- driven by (images,1s) 1.2198, (ctx,1s) 1.1139, (gen,1s) 1.0965. Baselines for contrast at 1s: ewma up to 1.479, naive 1.588, holt_winters 2.198. So the 'baseline rows darken' half is right and Chronos/Toto are genuinely within 3%; the blanket 'everywhere' fails only for TimesFM in the 1 s column. Adversarial defence considered and rejected: on a shading scale reaching 2.20 a cell at 1.22 is not white, and 22% is not 'a few percent' on any reading.
rulings.final_fix: Replace with: 'The Chronos-2 and Toto-2 rows are uniformly near-white --- within $3\%$ of the per-cell optimum in every cell --- and TimesFM within $6\%$ outside the \SI{1}{\second} column, where it reaches $22\%$ above best on images; the baseline rows darken as bins shrink.' (DB: max rel-to-best toto 1.006, chronos 1.030, timesfm 1.056 excluding 1s / 1.220 at (images,1s).)

rulings.quote: Toto-2 with covariates carries most column wins at \SI{15}{\second} and \SI{1}{\second}; Chronos-2 and TimesFM take the coarse-bin columns.
rulings.evidence: Query: `with c as (select variate,resolution,model,mode,wape from provenance.forecast_metrics where candidate='point' and h=-1 and span='common') select resolution,variate,(array_agg(model||'-'||mode order by wape))[1] from c group by 1,2;` Argmin per column: 15s -> toto-cov x4; 1s -> toto-cov (ctx,gen,requests), toto-uni (images); 30s -> toto-cov (ctx,gen), toto-uni (images,requests); 45s -> chronos-uni (ctx,requests), toto-cov (gen), toto-uni (images); 1min -> timesfm-uni (ctx), toto-cov (gen), chronos-cov (images), chronos-uni (requests). First clause is exactly right. Second clause overstates: Toto sweeps 30 s 4/4 and splits 45 s 2-2, so only the 1 min block goes mostly to Chronos/TimesFM. No number is wrong -- this is a scope/qualitative overstatement, hence DEFINITIONAL rather than THESIS_WRONG. All margins concerned are within 1.7% of the column best (chronos max rel 1.017 at 1min, timesfm 1.010).
rulings.final_fix: Replace with: 'Toto-2 carries every column win at \SI{15}{\second} and \SI{30}{\second} and three of four at \SI{1}{\second} (with covariates except on images); Chronos-2 and TimesFM take three of four at \SI{1}{\minute} and two of four at \SI{45}{\second}. Every one of these margins is within $2\%$ of the column best.'

rulings.quote: The HuggingFace-transformers eager forward (SDPA attention) runs $1.36$--$1.61\times$ above the composition, rising with $N$;
rulings.evidence: Query: `select n_images, ratio_meas_over_aic from provenance.collector_encoder_fn where source_path like '%anchor_dense_sdpa_2400%' and n_images in (1,8,32,64);` -> 1.3885, 1.3613, 1.5843, **1.6170**. The published table's SDPA cells (11.3/58.7/253.8/511.6) match this artifact and no other (anchor_sdpa_locked2400 would give 58.6 at N=8, not 58.7). Every candidate basis exceeds 1.615: unrounded 511.573/316.369 = 1.61701; table cells 511.6/316.4 = 1.61694; the 5x50 anchor 511.2617/316.369 = 1.6160; the oneworker burst5 row 511.601/316.369 = 1.6171. Dense-sweep max over N<=64 = **1.6208** (`select max(ratio_meas_over_aic) ... where source_path like '%anchor_dense_sdpa_2400%' and n_images<=64;`). A range upper bound must CONTAIN the measured maximum (bracketing precedent: ceil the high end), and 1.61 excludes 1.617 on every basis. This is truncation, not an ordinary rounding convention. Secondary: 'rising with $N$' is false from N=1 to N=8 (1.3885 -> 1.3613), so the published lower bound 1.36 is not the small-$N$ end of a monotone curve.
rulings.final_fix: Replace '$1.36$--$1.61\times$ above the composition, rising with $N$' with '$1.36$--$1.62\times$ above the composition, rising with $N$ above $N{=}8$'. Justification: anchor_dense_sdpa_2400 ratios 1.3885 / 1.3613 / 1.5843 / 1.6170 at N=1/8/32/64; 1.6170 -> 1.62 at two decimals on the unrounded and the published-cell basis alike.

rulings.quote: matches the composition to within $11.4\%$ ($-2.2\%,+11.3\%,+5.5\%$ at $N{=}8/32/64$)

All three published figures are the correctly rounded UNROUNDED residuals from one single artifact -- no mixing of rounded and unrounded bases occurs. The bound 'to within $11.4\%$' is a true upper bound on this basis (max 11.33%) and also on the dense-sweep basis (11.367%), so it is safe either way. Query: `select n_images,mean_ms,source_path from provenance.collector_encoder_fn where engine='vllm' and image_px=448 and source_path like '%vllm_eager_vit%';`
rulings.final_fix: NO EDIT. The tuple $(-2.2\%,+11.3\%,+5.5\%)$ is the correctly rounded unrounded-residual tuple against vllm_eager_vit.json. rulings.evidence: Query: `with s as (select n_images,mean_ms from provenance.collector_encoder_fn where source_path like '%anchor_dense_sdpa_2400%'), c as (select n_images,mean_ms from provenance.collector_encoder_fn where source_path like '%vit_compile_dense%') select s.n_images, s.mean_ms/c.mean_ms from s join c using(n_images) order by 1;` -> N=1 1.1213, 2 1.0627, 4 1.1514, 6 1.1708, 8 1.2035, 12 1.3210, 16 1.3411, 24 1.3986, 32 1.3646, 48 1.3751, 64 1.3802, 96 1.3897, 128 1.4022.
